subject: Avoid compile stan model every time a function is called

messages.author: afc5d1777b0456fc
messages.subject: Avoid compile stan model every time a function is called
parts:
Hi all,

I am a Master student who is currently writing an R package that uses stan as part of the functions. 
It all work fine, but just every time I call the function, it re-compiles the stan model, how do I write it such that it only compiles the first time unless I switch to another model? I have read in rstanarm one can pre-compile stan models in an R pacakge, but I may do that at a later stage..

NOTE: it only re-compiles if I do not assign the output to a name, i.e. foo.out<-fecr_stan(...) does not re-compile while fecr_stan(...) does.




A sample code is below:

fecr_stan<-function(preFEC,postFEC,rawCounts=FALSE,preCF=50,postCF=preCF,
                    paired=TRUE,zeroInflation=TRUE,
                    muPrior,phiPrior,deltaPrior,psiPrePrior,deltaPsiPrior,
                    nsamples=2000,nburnin=500,thinning=1,nchain=1,ncore=1,adaptdelta=0.9,verbose=FALSE){
   
  # set priors
  priors <- fecr_setPrior(muPrior=muPrior, phiPrior=phiPrior, deltaPrior=deltaPrior,
                         psiPrePrior=psiPrePrior, deltaPsiPrior=deltaPsiPrior)
  
  # set stan model
  if(paired & zeroInflation){code<-ZI_paired_stan(priors);model<-"Zero-inflated Bayesian model for paired design"}
  if(paired & !zeroInflation){code<-paired_stan(priors);model<-"Bayesian model without zero-inflation for paired design"}

  # create data list for stan use
  epg_data <-if(paired){
    list(J=preN, ystarbraw = preFEC, ystararaw = postFEC, fpre = preCF, fpost = postCF)
  } else {
      list(Jb=preN, Ja=postN, ystarbraw = preFEC, ystararaw = postFEC, fpre = preCF, fpost = postCF)}
  
  # whether or not to suppress progress information and errors
  stanModel <- stan_model(model_name=paste(model),model_code=code,auto_write = rstan_options("auto_write"=TRUE))
  if (verbose){
    samples <- sampling(stanModel,data=epg_data,iter=nsamples, warmup=nburnin, chains=nchain,
                        thin=thinning,control = list(adapt_delta = adaptdelta),cores=ncore)
   } else {
  samples <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(sampling(stanModel,data=epg_data,iter=nsamples, warmup=nburnin, chains=nchain,
                              thin=thinning,control = list(adapt_delta = adaptdelta),cores=ncore,refresh=-1)))}
  
  result <- ........
  cat("Model: ", model," ","Number of Samples: ",nsamples, " ","Warm-up samples: ",nburnin," ","Thinning: ",thinning," ")
  printSummary(result)
  return(invisible(samples))
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Avoid compile stan model every time a function is called
parts:
On Thursday, March 17, 2016 at 8:49:15 AM UTC-4, Craig Wang wrote:
NOTE: it only re-compiles if I do not assign the output to a name, i.e. foo.out<-fecr_stan(...) does not re-compile while fecr_stan(...) does.

That is correct. If a stanfit or stanmodel object is assigned to a symbol (that can easily be found), then calling the same Stan program does not recompile the model and instead fishes the compiled model out of the existing stanfit or stanmodel object. Otherwise, it has to recompile because loading the same dynamic shared object off of the disk crashes R.

Ben

messages.author: 5f5594be1382dc39
messages.subject: Re: Avoid compile stan model every time a function is called
parts:
Hi Ben,

I have a problem with RStudio crashing that seems like it might be to do with this. I started using rstan a few weeks ago and it's been great -- I've had no problems with it crashing RStudio at all. However, ever since I started calling stan() from inside a new function, this problem has appeared: the function runs fine the first time, it compiles the code and runs the chains and it's all lovely. Then I call the function again, with exactly the same arguments, and it crashes RStudio. I restart RStudio and everything works (pretty much) fine from then on. Sporadically it will fail after the first time, but I can generally run the function as many times as I like without it crashing.

I'm generating a new .stan file each time (I know you don't like me doing this, but I need to allow the user to specify general nonlinear models and I can't think of a good way to precompile). The function goes something like:

1) generate mymodel.stan from user-supplied character strings and save to working directory
2) run fit <- stan("mymodel.stan",...)
3) compute some stuff
4) return(list(fit=fit,...))

Is there something obvious about this approach that would cause problems with the way the DSO is reloaded, but only after I first compile the model and only if I try to quickly re-run it?

Thanks,
Will

stan_model("mymodel.stan")
stan("mymodel.stan",...)

in my function, it crashes first time. So it must be something to do with trying to compile the same model twice in quick succession and stan failing to recognise that the model's already been compiled. It doesn't seem to depend on extract() or summary(), because I can reproduce the crash by just calling
stan("mymodel.stan",...)
after first running my function.

Once I restart RStudio after the crash, everything runs fine and stan recognises that the model has been compiled already and goes straight into sampling.

Will
